sources.title: Environment, state and society in the central Himalayas to 1743
sources.note: Cambridge history chapter separating Kathmandu Valley history, diverse Himalayan societies, early Mallas, western states, and late eighteenth-century unification.

sources.title: Kingship, Buddhism and the Forging of a Region
sources.note: Archaeological study of thirteenth-century Khasa Malla formation, Sinja and Dullu, pilgrimage, routes, and west Himalayan regional interaction.

sources.title: Mediaeval History of Nepal, circa 750 to 1482
sources.note: Critical political chronology built from dated manuscripts, inscriptions, and chronicles; emphasizes severe source limits before the later fourteenth century.

sources.title: The Early Malla Period of Nepal
sources.note: Tribhuvan University article on the honorific Malla, early rulers, sparse records, and competing chronology from 1200 onward.

sources.title: Earthquakes in Nepali History
sources.note: Cambridge chapter critically presenting the 7 June 1255 chronicle account, aftershocks, displacement, royal death, and evidentiary limits.

sources.title: Sivadharma Manuscripts from Nepal and the Making of a Saiva Corpus
sources.note: Critical manuscript study and transcription of the 1201 Somadeva colophon, family beneficiaries, copying, donor merit, royal title, and religious coexistence.

sources.title: A 1216 Harihara manuscript colophon
sources.note: Printed Devanagari normalization, transliteration, and discussion of the dated Sanskrit post-colophon composed during Arimalladeva reign.

sources.title: An Ambitious Itinerary: Journey Across the Medieval Buddhist World in a Book
sources.note: Peer-reviewed manuscript study identifying an early thirteenth-century painted Sanskrit manuscript prepared at Sri Lham Mahavihara for monk Puspasena.

sources.title: Sinja Valley
sources.note: Nepal Department of Archaeology nomination describing Khasa capital remains, temples, settlement, pipes, Buddhist caves, inscriptions, and thirteenth-century script.

sources.title: The Sinja Valley Excavation in 2000
sources.note: Department of Archaeology journal report with trenches, rooms, pottery, glass, bones, drains, defenses, uncertainty, and radiocarbon range beginning 1270.

sources.title: Finding the Khasa Malla: Preliminary Investigations of the Surkhet Valley
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeological survey distinguishing Khasa Mallas from Valley Mallas, mapping inscriptions, languages, settlements, and west Himalayan political growth.

sources.title: Vajrayogini and early settlement of Sankhu
sources.note: Department of Archaeology nomination locating an early settlement on the Tibet route and warning that prominent surviving temple fabric is seventeenth century.

sources.title: Indigenous water management in Bhaktapur City
sources.note: Academic study of stone-spout chronology, canals, reuse, irrigation, neighborhood distribution, and the limits of projecting present systems backward.

sources.title: Susrutasamhita manuscript in the Memory of the World Register
sources.note: Institutional manuscript record describing date, palm leaf, script, medical scope, textual uniqueness, and survival in the Kaiser Library.

sources.title: The History of Ancient and Medieval Nepal
sources.note: Historical survey of early Malla chronology, education, manuscripts, monasteries, households, crafts, and trade, used with source and dating warnings.

sources.title: Handle with Intertwined Figures
sources.note: Museum record for a thirteenth-century Kathmandu Valley copper-alloy ritual-vessel handle with complex openwork naga imagery.

sources.title: Standing Lakshmi
sources.note: Museum record for a thirteenth-century Kathmandu Valley copper-alloy image inlaid with semiprecious stones.

sources.title: Astasahasrika Prajnaparamita manuscript leaf
sources.note: University repository record for a Nepalese Sanskrit manuscript leaf broadly dated 1200 to 1399 with later paintings over script.

sources.title: Reconciling the Varied Stories: Arniko Myths and Nationalization
sources.note: Peer-reviewed critique using a 1316 Yuan epitaph to reconstruct the artisan career while rejecting modern nationalist projection and invented appearance.

sources.title: Two Medieval Nepalese Buildings
sources.note: Architectural study distinguishing surviving, rebuilt, legendary, and securely dated fabric in Kathmandu Valley water and religious buildings.
